We strongly recommend that you install Antora within the playbook project rather than globally. Installing Antora locally makes it easier to manage the version of Antora. It also ensures that the version of Antora matches the version for which the playbook was made.
Now you’re ready to create your first playbook.

To produce a documentation site, Antora needs a playbook, which is defined using a playbook file. The simplest way to start using Antora is to point the playbook at existing documentation stored in remote repositories (i.e., content sources). For this example, we’ll use the content sources from the
Using your preferred text editor or IDE, create a new file and populate it with the configuration information
directory you made in the previous step.

site:
  title: Docs Site
  start_page: component-b::index.adoc

- url: https://gitlab.com/antora/demo/demo-component-a.git
    branches: HEAD
  - url: https://gitlab.com/antora/demo/demo-component-b.git
    branches: [v2.0, v1.0]
    start_path: docs
ui:
A page from a component version to be used as the home page for your site.
category contains the list of git repository locations, branch name patterns, and other repository properties that Antora uses when aggregating the site content.
category contains keys that specify the location of the UI bundle and how it should be processed.

Antora also supports local content sources, which are git repositories that have been cloned or otherwise initialized on the current machine. What that means is that it’s possible to create a site from a local repository that contains both the playbook and the content source(s) (i.e., a mono site). For this example, you can set up everything locally in the
directory created earlier without having to rely on any remote git repositories.

If you’re adding Antora to an existing local git repository, this step is not required.

Using your preferred text editor or IDE, create a the start page for the component version and populate it with a page title and some text.
Create one additional page so that you can study how the navigation is put together.

= New Page

You've found a new page.
Next, create a navigation file so that each page contains links to navigate to the other pages.
Notice that the start page for the component version is not included. That’s because it’s automatically added as the root of the navigation tree.
To finish putting together the content source root, create the component version descriptor,
. This file identifies a content source root and, in turn, defines a component version. We’ll create a versionless component named
, though you make this a versioned component or even the

name: project-name
version: ~
title: Project Name
nav:
- modules/ROOT/nav.adoc
Now that you have a local content source defined, you can create a playbook that uses it. Save the playbook file as

site:
  title: Docs Site
  start_page: project-name::index.adoc
content:
  sources:
  - url: .
    branches: HEAD
ui:
  bundle:
    url: https://gitlab.com/antora/antora-ui-default/-/jobs/artifacts/HEAD/raw/build/ui-bundle.zip?job=bundle-stable
    snapshot: true
This repository defines the start page for the component version we created as the start page for the site. The
key) isn’t required if the component version you created is the ROOT component.
Here’s how the file and directory structure inside the
directory should look when you’re done.

📒 docs-site
  📂 modules
    📂 ROOT
      📂 pages
        📄 index.adoc
        📄 new-page.adoc
      📄 nav.adoc
  📄 antora.yml
  📄 antora-playbook.yml
You can now generate the site as you did before.
